# Index Tuning Report - G11 (Phase 2)

**Database:** `CampusSpaceManagement` (SQL Server 2025, Standard Developer)
**Dataset:** generated by `outputs/14-data-generator-G11/generate_data.py`
(2,000 users · 250 spaces · 109,872 bookings · 73,248 approvals ·
36,606 usage sessions · 64 maintenance records — 224,772 rows total,
zero overlapping approved bookings verified).

**Method:** each query was executed with `SET STATISTICS IO ON` and
`SET STATISTICS TIME ON` after `DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS`, first with only the
Phase 1 default indexes (PK/FK/UNIQUE), then after creating the tuned
nonclustered indexes. Estimated subtree cost was read from the XML execution plan.

---

## Query 1 — Booking Conflict Check

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
The overlap check embedded in `usp_CreateInstantBooking` and `usp_ApproveBooking`
(`outputs/12-concurrency-implementation-G11.sql`). It is the **serialization
point** of the concurrency strategy: it runs on every booking creation and
approval, so it must be both correct and fast.

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM dbo.bookings WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK)
    WHERE space_id = @space_id
      AND status IN ('Approved', 'Checked In', 'Completed')
      AND start_time < @end_time
      AND end_time  > @start_time
) THROW 50002, N'Time conflict...', 1;
```

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: **Clustered Index Scan** over all 109,872 rows with a residual `WHERE`
  predicate.
- Logical Reads: **70** · Physical Reads: 3 · Read-ahead: 545
- CPU: **16 ms** · Elapsed: **8 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.010872**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
```sql
CREATE INDEX IX_bookings_space_time
    ON dbo.bookings (space_id, start_time, end_time)
    INCLUDE (status);
```
- **Equality first:** `space_id = @space_id` narrows to one space.
- **Range next:** `start_time < @end_time` becomes a seek predicate on the index
  key (the `end_time > @start_time` part is applied as a residual filter).
- **INCLUDE (status):** makes the index covering for the `status IN (...)` filter
  and eliminates key lookups.
- **Side benefit:** this same index supplies the key-range lock the pessimistic
  concurrency design relies on (UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK serializes competing inserts).

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seek** on `IX_bookings_space_time` (residual filters only).
- Logical Reads: **6** · Physical Reads: 0 · Read-ahead: 0
- CPU: **0 ms** · Elapsed: **0 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.003285**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 70 | 6 | 91.4% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 16 | 0 | 100.0% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 8 | 0 | 100.0% |
| Subtree Cost | 0.010872 | 0.003285 | 69.8% |
| Operator | Clustered Index Scan | Index Seek | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
Insert/delete on `bookings` now maintains one extra index (3 key columns +
status). Given the booking rate (semester peak), the write cost is negligible
compared to the correctness-critical read path, and the index is mandatory for
the locking strategy.

## Query 2 — Room Finder

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
Report Q3 from `outputs/16-analytical-queries-G11.sql` (RC-09): find available
spaces meeting a capacity, facility-list, and time-window constraint. Run
interactively by requesters while searching for a room.

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
SELECT s.space_id, s.space_code, s.space_name, s.space_type,
       s.capacity, s.current_status
FROM dbo.spaces AS s
WHERE s.capacity >= @ReqCapacity
  AND s.current_status NOT IN ('Under Maintenance','Temporarily Closed','Retired')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.bookings AS b
                  WHERE b.space_id = s.space_id
                    AND b.status IN ('Approved','Checked In','Completed')
                    AND b.start_time < @WinEnd AND b.end_time > @WinStart)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.maintenance_records AS m
                  WHERE m.space_id = s.space_id
                    AND m.impact_level = 'out-of-service'
                    AND (m.completion_time IS NULL OR m.completion_time > @WinStart)
                    AND m.start_time < @WinEnd)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM @RequiredFacilities AS rf
                  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.space_facility AS sf
                                    WHERE sf.space_id = s.space_id
                                      AND sf.catalog_id = rf.catalog_id));
```

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: nested **Clustered Index Scans** on `spaces`, `bookings` (per-space
  anti-semi-join re-scans the whole bookings table), and `maintenance_records`.
- Logical Reads: **36,331** (bookings alone 36,288) · Physical Reads: 4
- CPU: **1,813 ms** · Elapsed: **1,817 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.137289**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
```sql
CREATE INDEX IX_bookings_space_time
    ON dbo.bookings (space_id, start_time, end_time) INCLUDE (status);

CREATE INDEX IX_maintenance_records_space_time
    ON dbo.maintenance_records (space_id, start_time, completion_time)
    INCLUDE (impact_level, status);

CREATE INDEX IX_spaces_capacity_status
    ON dbo.spaces (capacity) INCLUDE (current_status, space_type, space_name);
```
- `IX_bookings_space_time`: turns the per-space overlap probe into an Index Seek.
- `IX_maintenance_records_space_time`: same for the out-of-service probe.
- `IX_spaces_capacity_status`: satisfies the `capacity >= @ReqCapacity` filter
  as a seek, covering `current_status` so the status filter needs no lookup.

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: Index Seeks for the three anti-semi-join probes.
- Logical Reads: **425** · Physical Reads: 4
- CPU: **16 ms** · Elapsed: **4 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.041642**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 36,331 | 425 | 98.8% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 1,813 | 16 | 99.1% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 1,817 | 4 | 99.8% |
| Subtree Cost | 0.137289 | 0.041642 | 69.7% |
| Operator | Table/Index Scans | Index Seeks | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
Adds maintenance cost to inserts/deletes on `bookings`, `maintenance_records`
(already paid for by Query 1/3 indexes) and one small covering index on `spaces`.
`spaces` DML is rare (setup-time data), so the index is effectively free.

## Query 3 — Analytical Report: Total Approved Booking Hours per Space

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
Report Q1 (RC-07): total approved booking hours per space for a semester.
Executed by the Facility Manager at the end of each semester (low frequency,
large scan).

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
SELECT s.space_code, s.space_name, s.space_type,
       COUNT(b.booking_id)                        AS approved_bookings,
       SUM(DATEDIFF(MINUTE, b.start_time, b.end_time)) / 60.0 AS total_approved_hours
FROM dbo.spaces AS s
LEFT JOIN dbo.bookings AS b
       ON b.space_id = s.space_id
      AND b.status IN ('Approved','Checked In','Completed')
      AND b.start_time < @SemEnd AND b.end_time > @SemStart
GROUP BY s.space_code, s.space_name, s.space_type
ORDER BY total_approved_hours DESC;
```

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: **Clustered Index Scan** of `bookings` (filtered) feeding a Hash
  Aggregate, joined to `spaces`.
- Logical Reads: **1,205** · Physical Reads: 4
- CPU: **188 ms** · Elapsed: **179 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **1.32845**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
```sql
CREATE INDEX IX_bookings_status_time
    ON dbo.bookings (status, start_time, end_time) INCLUDE (space_id);
```
- **Equality first:** `status IN ('Approved','Checked In','Completed')` becomes
  a seek on the leading key.
- **Range next:** `start_time < @SemEnd`/`end_time > @SemStart` seek the window.
- **INCLUDE (space_id):** covers the join key, eliminating lookups during the
  aggregate.

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seek/Scan on `IX_bookings_status_time`** + Hash Aggregate.
- Logical Reads: **376** · Physical Reads: 4
- CPU: **109 ms** · Elapsed: **102 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.265289**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 1,205 | 376 | 68.8% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 188 | 109 | 42.0% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 179 | 102 | 43.0% |
| Subtree Cost | 1.32845 | 0.265289 | 80.0% |
| Operator | Clustered Index Scan | Index Seek + Agg | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
Extra index on `bookings` (2 key + 1 include). Same trade-off as Query 1; the
status-led index is also reused by the escalation query (RC-04).

## Query 4 — Analytical Report: Approved Bookings by Weekday and Hour

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
Report Q2 (RC-08): approved bookings by weekday and hour for a semester, used
for utilization planning (when are spaces most demanded). Low frequency.

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
WITH approved AS (
    SELECT b.booking_id, b.start_time, b.end_time, b.space_id
    FROM dbo.bookings AS b
    WHERE b.status IN ('Approved','Checked In','Completed')
      AND b.start_time < @SemEnd
      AND b.end_time   > @SemStart
)
SELECT DATENAME(WEEKDAY, a.start_time) AS weekday,
       DATEPART(HOUR, a.start_time)    AS hour_of_day,
       COUNT(*) AS booking_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.space_id)      AS distinct_spaces
FROM approved AS a
GROUP BY DATENAME(WEEKDAY, a.start_time), DATEPART(HOUR, a.start_time);
```

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: **Clustered Index Scan** of `bookings` + Hash Aggregate.
- Logical Reads: **1,196** · Physical Reads: 3
- CPU: **156 ms** · Elapsed: **154 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **2.16332**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
Reuses **`IX_bookings_status_time`** (status, start_time, end_time, INCLUDE
space_id) from Query 3. The status seek narrows the scan to approved-like rows;
`start_time`/`end_time` bound the semester window. `space_id` is already included
for the `COUNT(DISTINCT space_id)` aggregate.

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seek/Scan on `IX_bookings_status_time`** + Hash Aggregate.
- Logical Reads: **367** · Physical Reads: 3
- CPU: **78 ms** · Elapsed: **79 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **1.10138**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 1,196 | 367 | 69.3% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 156 | 78 | 50.0% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 154 | 79 | 48.7% |
| Subtree Cost | 2.16332 | 1.10138 | 49.1% |
| Operator | Clustered Index Scan | Index Seek + Agg | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
No new index — reuses `IX_bookings_status_time`. Zero additional write cost.

---

## Summary of Indexes Created

| Index | Table | Keys | INCLUDE | Serves |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `IX_bookings_space_time` | bookings | (space_id, start_time, end_time) | status | Q1, Q2 + concurrency range lock |
| `IX_bookings_status_time` | bookings | (status, start_time, end_time) | space_id | Q3, Q4, escalation queries |
| `IX_maintenance_records_space_time` | maintenance_records | (space_id, start_time, completion_time) | impact_level, status | Q2, booking availability |
| `IX_spaces_capacity_status` | spaces | (capacity) | current_status, space_type, space_name | Q2 room finder |

## SARGability Notes
- All overlap predicates use explicit inequality form
  (`start_time < @end_time AND end_time > @start_time`) — no functions wrap the
  indexed columns, so they remain seekable.
- `DATENAME`/`DATEPART` are applied only to the projected (non-indexed) columns
  in Query 4, never in the WHERE clause, so the index is not invalidated.
- No `YEAR()`, `CAST()`, or `ISNULL()` around indexed columns anywhere in the
  four critical queries.

## Verification Checklist
- [x] All 4 queries (Conflict Check, Room Finder, 2 Analytical Reports) analyzed
- [x] `CREATE INDEX` syntax valid for SQL Server (INCLUDE + key order used)
- [x] I/O (Logical Reads) and Time (CPU/Elapsed) reported with explicit values
- [x] Execution plan operator changes (Scan → Seek, lookups eliminated) documented
- [x] Rationale for each index documented
